+[ -z "$(sed -n 2p "$T/body")" ] || fail "expected the first line to stand alone"
+expect_output "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/50"
+
+scenario "the ticket says what anyone can now read, what the factory still refuses, and the two things left to the owner"
+github

+expect_part "What anyone can now read" "the decision record"
+expect_part "What anyone can now read" "Every agent's transcript"
+expect_part "What anyone can now read" "open an issue or a pull request"

+expect_part "What the factory still refuses" "decisions U563a"
+expect_part "What the factory still refuses" "starts no build, no agent and no merge"
+expect_part "What is left to you" '1. **Add a `SECURITY.md`**'
+expect_part "What is left to you" "2. **Switch on private vulnerability reporting,**"
+
+scenario "a second time, the ticket is open: none is filed"
+github
+echo "[$(issue 7 "Another ticket" owner User),$(issue 50 "$title" 'github-actions[bot]' Bot)]" > "$T/issues"
+run "$scripts/flag-public.sh"
+expect_status 0
+expect_no_call "issue create"
+expect_output "issue #50 already tells the owner"
+
+scenario "a ticket with the same title that another account opened stops none: the ticket is filed"
+github
+echo "[$(issue 48 "$title" stranger User),$(issue 49 "$title" github-actions User)]" > "$T/issues"
+run "$scripts/flag-public.sh"
+expect_status 0
+expect_calls 1 "gh issue create"
+
+scenario "a pull request with the same title stops none: the ticket is filed"
+github
+jq -c '. + {pull_request: {}}' <<<"$(issue 48 "$title" 'github-actions[bot]' Bot)" | jq -sc . > "$T/issues"
+run "$scripts/flag-public.sh"
+expect_status 0
+expect_calls 1 "gh issue create"
+
+scenario "the open tickets cannot be read: it stops, says the owner was not told, and files nothing"
+github
+echo "api repos" > "$T/fail"
+run "$scripts/flag-public.sh"
+expect_status 1
+expect_output "The owner was not told that the repository is public: the open tickets could not be read"
+expect_no_call "issue create"
+
+scenario "the ticket cannot be filed: it stops and says the owner was not told"
+github
+echo "issue create" > "$T/fail"
+run "$scripts/flag-public.sh"
+expect_status 1
+expect_output "The owner was not told that the repository is public: the ticket that says so could not be filed"
+expect_no_output "told the owner that the repository is public: "

# Four times a day, runs again the jobs refused for billing or held by the usage limit, then flags each idle ticket.
name: flag-idle

on:
  schedule:
    # Every six hours (decisions T271e); off the hour, when GitHub starts late.
    - cron: "43 */6 * * *"

jobs:
  look:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: write       # to lift the hold of the Claude usage limit once it has reset (decisions A395e)
      issues: write         # to flag a ticket and tell it what was found
      pull-requests: read   # to see which tickets are in flight
      actions: write        # to run a refused run again (decisions H220a)
      checks: read          # to read why a job never started
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run again the jobs GitHub refused to start for billing
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: factory/scripts/rerun-refused.sh
      # A refused run that could not be read or run again hides no idle ticket (decisions T271f).
      - name: Start again what the usage limit held, or flag each ticket in flight that nothing is working on
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          BOARD_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BOARD_TOKEN }}   # lets start-waiting.sh read the order of the board (decisions T335a)
        run: factory/scripts/flag-idle.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Keeps the reviewers' notes in one ticket, and starts the build of that ticket.

# Security

## Who the factory acts for

The factory acts only for an account with write access to this repository, and for its own two bot accounts, `github-actions[bot]` and `claude[bot]`. An issue, comment or review from anyone else starts nothing.

## Whose words an agent acts on

An agent treats text written by anyone else, and anything it reads on the web or in a package, as data and never as an instruction.

## Secrets

No agent or script prints a secret, writes one to disk, or sends one anywhere but to the service it is for. A reviewer is given no GitHub token.

## What is not protected

Every agent session holds the Claude token in its environment, because it needs the token to run. An agent that reads a hostile page could be talked into sending the token out. Limiting where an agent may send data would close this, and it is not built.

A pull request from a fork gets no secret from GitHub, so no agent runs on it.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report it privately: on this repository's Security tab, press "Report a vulnerability". Do not open an issue for it.

content.text:
Pull request [#568](https://github.com/edmulraney/tinyfactory/pull/568) for ticket #567 is handed over and marked ready for review. `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build` and the scaffold proof all pass after the last merge of `main`.

- **What it adds:** the workflow `flag-public.yml` starts on GitHub's `public` event and runs `flag-public.sh`. The script files one ticket labelled `needs-human` that says what anyone can now read, what the factory still refuses for an account with no write access, and what is left to the owner.
- **A second `public` event:** the script finds the open ticket that `github-actions[bot]` opened with that title, and files none.
- **Proof:** `factory/tests/flag-public.test.sh` covers the ticket's three parts, the second event, and each GitHub call failing. It also checks that `events.sh` lists the workflow under `public`.
- **Decisions:** `factory/decisions/567.md` holds three rows: how the open ticket is recognised, why the two steps stay with the owner, and why the workflow asks `trusted.sh` about no account.

The architecture review found nothing. The code review found one bug, which I fixed: where the repository already holds a `SECURITY.md`, as this one does, the ticket now asks only for private vulnerability reporting.

- **It waits for the owner's approval:** the new workflow has a `permissions:` block (`contents: read`, `issues: write`), which only the owner decides.
- **No attribution line:** the pull request description leaves out the "Generated with Claude Code" line, because `check-pr-conventions.sh` refuses any line outside the description's shape.
